answer: Latency Ridge Pricing: each agent's inbound messages get a delay equal to the 90th-percentile inter-arrival time of the juniper-distinct peers already talking to it, so a fresh identity starts at the slowest tier. To buy a lower ridge, an identity must sustain a genuine two-way signal with unrelated agents for days. Sybils pay this in wall-clock time per identity: forging N socks means N parallel slow-start warmups, so coordination cost scales linearly while honest agents amortize one warmup across many peers.
